name: 800G/1.6T optical transceivers
description_md: AI clusters are as much networks as computers: a 100k-GPU cluster needs hundreds of thousands of optical transceivers, and each GPU generation doubles the port speed. 800G shipments are set to more than double in 2026 while 1.6T — required for Rubin-class scale-up fabrics — is only beginning to ramp from a small base; the transceiver market is forecast to hit ~$26B in 2026, +60% y/y. US-listed suppliers are at record levels: Coherent's datacenter & comms revenue grew 41% y/y to ~75% of the company, and Lumentum posted record 800G revenue with 1.6T ramping and demand reported above supply — Nvidia has taken equity stakes in both, a signal of how critical (and tight) the layer is. The binding sub-constraint is upstream components: EML/CW laser chips and indium-phosphide capacity, where Coherent and Lumentum are two of only a handful of merchant sources. Status basis: judged binding — component (laser) supply and 1.6T qualification pace, not assembly, cap cluster deployment schedules; vendors themselves describe demand above supply. Softens toward 'easing' if InnoLight/Eoptolink capacity and CPO adoption catch up in 2027.

controlled_by.share_note: Top-3 datacom transceiver maker and key merchant EML/laser source; DC & comms ~75% of revenue, +41% y/y (disclosed)
Key laser/transceiver supplier; record 800G, 1.6T ramping, demand above supply (company_claimed). InnoLight (largest, China) and Eoptolink share the module market

dependents.dependency_md: Every NVLink/Spectrum-X scale-out fabric consumes multiple optics per GPU; Nvidia holds equity stakes in both Coherent and Lumentum to secure the layer, and its co-packaged-optics roadmap depends on the same laser suppliers.
TPU pods and Google's Jupiter fabric are among the largest 800G/1.6T consumers; optics availability paces datacenter network upgrades.
Hyperion-class clusters require transceivers in the millions of units; Meta buys across InnoLight/Coherent/Eoptolink and is exposed to any EML shortage.

substitutes_md: More second sources than most compute bottlenecks — InnoLight (largest), Eoptolink, and a broad Chinese module ecosystem — but module assembly is not the constraint; laser dies and InP wafer capacity are, and those are concentrated in Coherent, Lumentum, and a few Japanese suppliers. Alternatives: copper (only within-rack reach), linear-drive/LPO optics (cheaper, same lasers), and co-packaged optics (TSMC/Broadcom/Nvidia, volume ~2027-28 — which shifts the bottleneck to TSMC rather than relieving it). Qualification cycles for a new optics vendor on a hyperscale fabric run ~2-4 quarters.
downcycle_md: Optics is historically the whipsaw layer: modules are ordered ahead of cluster builds, inventories balloon late-cycle, and pricing falls fast (800G ASPs already decline double-digits annually even in shortage). Contracts are mostly rolling POs, not take-or-pay — hyperscalers can cut orders within quarters, as they did to the 400G complex in 2022-23. In a downturn, Chinese module makers with commodity cost structures would keep share while Coherent/Lumentum see the specialty laser premium compress; Nvidia's equity stakes would cushion strategy, not P&L. The 1.6T ramp would be the first casualty since it serves only frontier clusters.
